card.title: No. 46 COMMANDO
card.text: Deployment: Add a BLAST and a PLAN to your hand.
card.flavorText: No. 46 Royal Marine Commando was formed in August 1943 as the Royal Marines Division was being turned into commando units. Led by Lieutenant Colonel Campbell Hardy, it trained for the demanding role of light assault infantry. Like other commandos, its men passed through the course at Achnacarry in the Scottish Highlands, where they practiced forced marches, weapons handling, map reading, climbing, small boat work, and demolitions. The unit landed in Normandy on 6 June 1944 and fought on the Orne River bridgehead beside the British 6th Airborne Division. It entered Douvres-la-Délivrande two days later, a moment captured in a wartime photograph showing local civilians watching the commandos move through the village. Heavy losses in Normandy forced No. 46 Commando back to Britain for refitting in late 1944. It returned to mainland Europe in January 1945, guarded Antwerp, then j participated in river-crossing assaults during the advance into Germany. After being assigned to occupation duties, it was disbanded in 1946.
